questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to save enough money to buy your first house
Why people in the UK have so little money saved
How the meaning of 'thrift' has changed over time
The dangers of borrowing money from banks
questions.why: The programme is all about 'thrift' and its changing meanings through history.

questions.q: Why is Sam trying to limit his spending?
options: He is saving for a house deposit
He has lost his job
He wants to go on holiday
He is paying back a loan
questions.why: Sam says he is saving up for a deposit to buy a house.

questions.q: According to Alison Hulme, what did the oldest meaning of 'thrift' describe?
options: Being careful with money
Giving money to the poor
Working hard every day
Living well and flourishing
questions.why: She says the older definition comes from 'thrive' and meant the ability to live well and flourish.

questions.q: Why did the Puritans think people should save money?
options: To become rich
To give to others in need
To pay for wars
To buy land
questions.why: Neil says they believed people ought to save money in order to give to others in need.

questions.q: What was thrift connected to in the Victorian era?
options: Avoiding waste to help the country's war effort
A religious duty to give money to the church
Managing your money to be a responsible citizen
Buying expensive luxury products to show wealth
questions.why: Sam says it was about managing your own money in order to be a responsible citizen.

questions.q: How did ideas about thrift change during the Second World War?
options: People were asked to avoid waste to help the war
People were told to spend more to help shops
Saving money in a bank became illegal for a time
Thrift was no longer discussed in newspapers
questions.why: Sam says the public was encouraged to avoid waste so every resource could go into the war effort.

questions.q: What view does Alison Hulme NOT fully agree with?
options: That consumer capitalism exists in the developed world
That thrift has several different definitions today
That the Puritans valued frugality and hard work
That people slid morally into consumerism
questions.why: She describes the 'moral slide into consumerism' idea and says, “It's not a view that I subscribe to.”

questions.q: What is Alison Hulme's conclusion about thrift today?
options: It has disappeared completely from modern life
It hasn't declined, even though consumerism has grown
It only exists among a few religious groups today
It is stronger than ever before in rich countries
questions.why: She says there's been a rise in consumer capitalism, 'but thrift hasn't declined.'
